read_file.description: Read a UTF-8 text file. Existing workspace paths take precedence; missing relative paths fall back to a unique readable file in assigned skill roots. Use skill to select an assigned skill explicitly.

path.description: Workspace-first file path, or a relative path inside the explicitly selected skill.

skill.description: Optional assigned skill name. Resolves path only inside that skill; path must be relative and remain inside its root.

write_file.description: Write UTF-8 text to a file relative to the working directory.

bash.description: Run a shell command in the working directory.

activate_skill.description: Load the full instructions for an allowed skill.

list_available_tools.description: List installed native and artifact tool names, descriptions, and session access without executing or granting access. Access states do not guarantee policy approval.

request_tool.description: Request a tool be added to this subagent for the current session.

reason.description: Why the task needs this tool.

tool_authoring.description: Create and activate a user-owned tool artifact that runs with an available command-line runtime.

replace_invalid.description: Recreate an existing invalid artifact with a complete replacement and separate direct user confirmation. Preserves the original in an INVALID_ archive, including if installation then fails; no automatic rollback. Valid and native tools are protected.

input_schema.description: Valid JSON Schema for tool arguments with explicit root type object; define named inputs under properties and required as an array of property names.

files.description: Relative file paths mapped to text contents; may use any language supported by the selected runtime.

command.description: Exec argv array, not shell text: keep executable and each argument separate, e.g. ["python3", "{artifact_dir}/main.py"]. Paths with spaces remain a single entry. Creation validates the definition without executing or verifying behavior. Run approved representative input and compare the requested result before claiming completion. Runs in the target project; use {artifact_dir} for bundled files and {workspace_dir} for the project. JSON arguments arrive on stdin. HARNESS_SKILL_DIRS contains allowed skill paths as JSON.
